answer: Make standing pass through one narrow vertex: a single shared verification gate that admits only a few identities per epoch, its places sold by sealed bids of locked time. A lone agent bids once. A farm bidding for fifty masks bids against itself at every turn of the queue — each extra mask raises what its siblings must pay, until the price hardens like marble and the farm's margin cracks like a walnut shell. Cloning cannot outrun a gate that serves one at a time; the queue, not the mint, decides how many may stand.
